union.summary: `getUsedBounds()` added as a required member of the `Store` interface; any implementation not updated in this diff will throw `store.getUsedBounds is not a function` from `Sheet.getUsedBounds()` during calculation

union.summary: Blank-cell skipping in `Arguments.iterate` applies to every range-consuming function, not just aggregations, silently changing/breaking positional and blank-counting semantics

union.summary: `resolveRange` inverts the range when the explicit `from` endpoint lies beyond the sheet's used bounds, so the expanded range silently includes cells *before* the requested start

union.summary: Deleting/clearing the bottom-most or right-most populated cell shrinks the used bounds, so the rebuilt dependants map no longer contains that cell and whole-column/row formulas keep a stale value

Mirror of the added test 'picks up a newly added cell beyond the prior data extent': after A10=5 the map contains A10→D1, but when A10 is cleared the map is rebuilt with maxR back to 3, so A10 is no longer a key and the edit to A10 has no dependants — `=SUM(A:A)` in D1 is never marked dirty and keeps showing 65 instead of 60. union.summary: YorkieStore expands formulas with index-only bounds that ignore `batchOverlay`, so during a batch (e.g. paste) new cells outside the prior extent are neither summed nor registered as dependencies

union.summary: Dependants map now materializes every cell of every expanded whole-column/row range via `toSrefs`, which is O(rows×cols) per formula and can hang/OOM on realistic sheets

union.summary: `CellIndex.bounds()` can return `Infinity`/`-Infinity` coordinates or an inflated extent because it trusts key presence rather than non-empty buckets and assumes rowIndex/colIndex are both populated

union.summary: Rebuilding the formula string from `extractTokens` output can corrupt formulas whose token text is not verbatim source (whitespace runs, quoted string literals)
union.evidence: formula.ts `expandUnboundedRanges` concatenates `token.text` for every token and prepends `'='` (`return '=' + body;`). This is only safe if `extractTokens` returns strictly verbatim text for every token and covers all gaps — the grammar `-> skip`s WS, and STRING tokens are also used as gap fillers, so any normalization (dropped whitespace, unquoted string text) silently rewrites the user's formula whenever a single unbounded ref is present. It also assumes tokens exclude the leading '='; if not, the result is '==…'.

union.summary: `resolveRange` throws on cross-sheet input that `isUnboundedRange` happily accepts — an inconsistent contract waiting for the next caller
union.evidence: `isUnboundedRange` strips the sheet prefix via `parseCrossSheetRef(...).localRef`, but `resolveRange` does `srng.split(':')` and feeds `'Sheet2!A'` to `parsePartialRef`, whose regex `^([A-Za-z]*)([0-9]*)$` cannot match, so it throws 'Invalid Reference'. Only the `isCrossSheetRef` pre-check in `expandUnboundedRanges` keeps this from firing today; both functions are exported.

union.summary: Aggregations over an all-blank expanded range now receive zero arguments, so AVERAGE/MIN/MAX can produce NaN or an error where they previously returned 0
union.evidence: With the new skip in `Arguments.iterate`, `=AVERAGE(A:A)` on an empty sheet (expanded to `A1:A1`, blank) yields no values at all; a naive `sum/count` gives 0/0. Only `=SUM(A:A)` on an empty sheet is covered by the new tests (`expects '0'`).

union.summary: `calculate()` re-reads used bounds per formula cell inside the loop, so bounds can change mid-pass (spill writes) and disagree with the bounds used to build the dependency order
union.evidence: calculator.ts: `const formula = expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f!, await sheet.getUsedBounds());` sits inside the per-cell loop. Spill results written earlier in the same pass extend the used extent, so later formulas expand against different bounds than the ones the topological order was derived from — a formula can end up referencing a cell scheduled after it, yielding a stale value for that pass.

union.summary: `isUnboundedRange` ignores extra colon-separated segments and does not reject empty endpoints
union.evidence: `const [from, to] = local.split(':');` discards anything past the second segment, and `isFullRef('')` returns false, so a malformed `':A1'` or `'A1:B2:C3'` is classified as unbounded and handed to `resolveRange`, which then relies on the try/catch in `expandUnboundedRanges`.

union.summary: `resolveRange` silently inverts open-ended ranges whose explicit start lies beyond the sheet's used extent, pulling in cells before the start
union.evidence: `resolveRange` builds `to` as `{ r: b.r ?? max.r, c: b.c ?? max.c }` and then calls `toRange(from, to)`, which normalizes (sorts) the endpoints. If the `from` endpoint is beyond the data extent, e.g. `=SUM(A5:A)` with bounds maxR=3, we get from={r:5,c:1}, to={r:3,c:1}, and `toRange` flips it into A3:A5 — a range that includes A3 and A4, i.e. cells *above* the requested start. With the issue's data (A1=10,A2=20,A3=30) `=SUM(A5:A)` returns 30 instead of 0, and `=AVERAGE(B4:B)` returns 200 instead of an empty/DIV0 result. The same happens for row-open forms (`A:B5` style / `5:` variants) whenever the explicit endpoint exceeds `bounds`.

union.summary: Blank-cell skipping in `Arguments.iterate` changes semantics for *all* bounded ranges, breaking position-dependent and paired-range functions
union.evidence: The new block `const isRange = isSrng(node.v); ... if (isRange) { const cell = grid.get(ref); if (!cell || cell.v === undefined || cell.v === '') continue; }` is applied to every range argument, not just expanded unbounded ones. Any function whose semantics depend on the *number* or *ordinal position* of cells in a range (MATCH/INDEX-style lookups, COUNTBLANK, ROWS/COLUMNS-ish helpers, or paired ranges such as SUMIF(range, crit, sum_range) / SUMPRODUCT) now receives a compacted, misaligned stream: e.g. `=MATCH(x, A1:A10, 0)` returns the index within the non-blank subset, not within the range. union.summary: Whole-column/whole-row expansion can include the formula's own cell, creating a self-reference the engine never had to handle
union.evidence: `expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f!, await sheet.getUsedBounds())` clamps to bounds computed *including the formula cell itself*. `=SUM(1:1)` entered in D1 expands to `SUM(A1:D1)`, and `=SUM(A:A)` entered in A5 expands to `SUM(A1:A5)` — the formula depends on itself. `buildDependantsMap` will then record `A5 -> {A5}` (self edge), which either trips the cycle path or re-dirties the cell indefinitely. Excel reports a circular reference here; the new tests deliberately place every formula outside the referenced column/row (`=SUM(1:1)` at r2c4, `=SUM(A:A)` at c4), so this path is untested.

union.summary: Shrinking the used bounds (clearing the last populated cell) leaves formulas over unbounded ranges stale
union.evidence: `buildDependantsMap` computes `const bounds = this.cellIndex.bounds()` *after* the edit has been applied, then expands each formula against those bounds. When the edit deletes the cell that defined the extent (e.g. A10 cleared while `=SUM(A:A)` exists), bounds have already shrunk to r<=3, so the formula's dependency set is A1:A3 and does not contain A10; the dirty cell A10 therefore has no dependants and the formula is never recalculated, keeping the pre-delete total on screen. The new test only covers the growth direction ('picks up a newly added cell beyond the prior data extent'), not deletion. Same logic in YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap.

union.summary: YorkieStore bounds ignore `batchOverlay`, so batched writes expand unbounded ranges against stale extents
union.evidence: `getUsedBounds()` and the new `const bounds = this.cellIndex.bounds()` in `buildDependantsMap` read only the committed cell index; the `batchOverlay` branch immediately below iterates overlay cells (`for (const [sref, cell] of this.batchOverlay)`) and expands their formulas with those same committed bounds. Cells written/removed in the overlay (e.g. a paste extending column A far past the old extent, or an overlay deletion at the extent) are not reflected, so dependency edges and the expanded range both miss them and `=SUM(A:A)` computes over the pre-batch extent.

union.summary: Newly lexable `A:A` / `1:1` REFERENCE tokens reach un-updated consumers that call parseRef/parseRange and will throw
union.evidence: The grammar change makes `A:A`, `1:1`, `A1:B` lex as REFERENCE tokens everywhere, but only three call sites were given the `expandUnboundedRanges` guard (calculator, MemStore.buildDependantsMap, YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap). Every other consumer of REFERENCE tokens still parses them directly: `extractFormulaRanges` (parses each REFERENCE via parseRange for highlighting — the docs added in this diff *claim* it 'skips unbounded refs' although no code in the diff makes it skip), `toSrefs(extractReferences(f))` used outside those three sites, `shiftFormula`/`shiftSref` (row/column insert, fill, copy-paste rewriting) and `normalizeFormulaOnCommit`. `parseRef('A')` / `parseRef('1')` throw 'Invalid Reference', so typing `=SUM(A:A)` in the formula bar or inserting a row near such a formula can throw an unhandled exception in the UI rather than degrade.

union.summary: `CellIndex.bounds()` can return Infinity coordinates and trusts index keys that may outlive their cells
union.evidence: The empty check only tests `this.rowIndex.size === 0`; if `colIndex` is empty (or is emptied independently) while `rowIndex` is not, minC/maxC stay `Infinity`/`-Infinity` and the returned Range contains non-finite coordinates, which `resolveRange`/`toSrng` will turn into a garbage reference. Likewise, if deletion leaves zero-size buckets in `rowIndex`/`colIndex`, `bounds()` over-reports the extent and unbounded ranges expand over phantom rows/columns.

union.summary: `resolveRange` throws on cross-sheet input and ignores extra `:` segments
union.evidence: `resolveRange` does `srng.split(':')` with no cross-sheet handling, so `resolveRange("Sheet2!A:A", bounds)` sends 'Sheet2!A' into `parsePartialRef`, whose regex `^([A-Za-z]*)([0-9]*)$` fails and throws 'Invalid Reference'. It is exported alongside `isUnboundedRange` (which *does* strip the sheet prefix), so the asymmetry invites throwing call sites; the caller in formula.ts only avoids it by an explicit `!isCrossSheetRef` check. Quoted sheet names containing ':' would also mis-split.

union.summary: `expandUnboundedRanges` rebuilds the formula by concatenating token texts, relying on `extractTokens` round-tripping exactly
union.evidence: `let body = ''; for (const token of tokens) { ... body += token.text } return '=' + body;` reconstructs the whole formula from tokens. Any text the lexer drops or normalizes (hidden-channel whitespace, or a gap-filling STRING token whose `text` is not byte-identical to the source) is silently lost from the rewritten formula that is then evaluated — and if `extractTokens` ever emits the leading '=' as a token the result becomes '==...'. The rewrite also only runs when `formula.startsWith('=')`, so any stored formula lacking the '=' prefix keeps its unbounded refs and evaluates to #ERROR!.

union.summary: Used bounds are re-read per cell inside the calculation loop, so expansion is inconsistent within one pass
union.evidence: `await sheet.getUsedBounds()` is invoked inside the per-cell body of `calculate`, after earlier iterations may have written spill values that extend the extent. Two `=SUM(A:A)` cells in the same recalculation can therefore be expanded against different bounds, producing divergent results for identical formulas in one pass (plus a repeated async read per cell).

When the edit deletes the cell that defined the extent (e.g. A10 cleared while `=SUM(A:A)` exists), bounds have already shrunk to r<=3, so the formula's dependency set is A1:A3 and does not contain A10; the dirty cell A10 therefore has no dependants and the formula is never recalculated, keeping the pre-delete total on screen. The new test only covers the growth direction ('picks up a newly added cell beyond the prior data extent'), not deletion. Same logic in YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap.

per_sample.summary: YorkieStore bounds ignore `batchOverlay`, so batched writes expand unbounded ranges against stale extents
per_sample.evidence: `getUsedBounds()` and the new `const bounds = this.cellIndex.bounds()` in `buildDependantsMap` read only the committed cell index; the `batchOverlay` branch immediately below iterates overlay cells (`for (const [sref, cell] of this.batchOverlay)`) and expands their formulas with those same committed bounds. Cells written/removed in the overlay (e.g. a paste extending column A far past the old extent, or an overlay deletion at the extent) are not reflected, so dependency edges and the expanded range both miss them and `=SUM(A:A)` computes over the pre-batch extent.

per_sample.summary: Newly lexable `A:A` / `1:1` REFERENCE tokens reach un-updated consumers that call parseRef/parseRange and will throw
per_sample.evidence: The grammar change makes `A:A`, `1:1`, `A1:B` lex as REFERENCE tokens everywhere, but only three call sites were given the `expandUnboundedRanges` guard (calculator, MemStore.buildDependantsMap, YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap). Every other consumer of REFERENCE tokens still parses them directly: `extractFormulaRanges` (parses each REFERENCE via parseRange for highlighting — the docs added in this diff *claim* it 'skips unbounded refs' although no code in the diff makes it skip), `toSrefs(extractReferences(f))` used outside those three sites, `shiftFormula`/`shiftSref` (row/column insert, fill, copy-paste rewriting) and `normalizeFormulaOnCommit`. `parseRef('A')` / `parseRef('1')` throw 'Invalid Reference', so typing `=SUM(A:A)` in the formula bar or inserting a row near such a formula can throw an unhandled exception in the UI rather than degrade.

per_sample.summary: `CellIndex.bounds()` can return Infinity coordinates and trusts index keys that may outlive their cells
per_sample.evidence: The empty check only tests `this.rowIndex.size === 0`; if `colIndex` is empty (or is emptied independently) while `rowIndex` is not, minC/maxC stay `Infinity`/`-Infinity` and the returned Range contains non-finite coordinates, which `resolveRange`/`toSrng` will turn into a garbage reference. Likewise, if deletion leaves zero-size buckets in `rowIndex`/`colIndex`, `bounds()` over-reports the extent and unbounded ranges expand over phantom rows/columns.

per_sample.summary: `resolveRange` throws on cross-sheet input and ignores extra `:` segments
per_sample.evidence: `resolveRange` does `srng.split(':')` with no cross-sheet handling, so `resolveRange("Sheet2!A:A", bounds)` sends 'Sheet2!A' into `parsePartialRef`, whose regex `^([A-Za-z]*)([0-9]*)$` fails and throws 'Invalid Reference'. It is exported alongside `isUnboundedRange` (which *does* strip the sheet prefix), so the asymmetry invites throwing call sites; the caller in formula.ts only avoids it by an explicit `!isCrossSheetRef` check. Quoted sheet names containing ':' would also mis-split.

per_sample.summary: `expandUnboundedRanges` rebuilds the formula by concatenating token texts, relying on `extractTokens` round-tripping exactly
per_sample.evidence: `let body = ''; for (const token of tokens) { ... body += token.text } return '=' + body;` reconstructs the whole formula from tokens. Any text the lexer drops or normalizes (hidden-channel whitespace, or a gap-filling STRING token whose `text` is not byte-identical to the source) is silently lost from the rewritten formula that is then evaluated — and if `extractTokens` ever emits the leading '=' as a token the result becomes '==...'. The rewrite also only runs when `formula.startsWith('=')`, so any stored formula lacking the '=' prefix keeps its unbounded refs and evaluates to #ERROR!.

per_sample.summary: Used bounds are re-read per cell inside the calculation loop, so expansion is inconsistent within one pass
per_sample.evidence: `await sheet.getUsedBounds()` is invoked inside the per-cell body of `calculate`, after earlier iterations may have written spill values that extend the extent. Two `=SUM(A:A)` cells in the same recalculation can therefore be expanded against different bounds, producing divergent results for identical formulas in one pass (plus a repeated async read per cell).
